facts.statement: Case property is 4 Thistlewick Rise, Larkcombe, ZZ1 1ZZ; tenant Nessa Quill, landlord Orin Vale.
Tenant reported on 04 Sep 2025 a recurring leak behind the shower after an earlier pipe tightening failed, with water through the grout and worsening damage to the wall covering.
Landlord's approval on 07 Sep covered arranging a plumbing inspection and obtaining a quote only; it did not authorise repair work.
No landlord standing spend cap is on file in this case, so the default cap of £0 applies and any spend requires the landlord's own approval.

Tenant authorised office-key access on 15 Sep while away and asked for the visit as soon as possible; the contractor offered Thursday late morning and the inspection took place, as a quotation followed on 18 Sep.

Quotation NBL-001-Q1 dated 18 Sep 2025: scope is removal of screen, bath taps and shower valve; wall-and-riser cladding with chrome trims; new bath taps and shower valve; refit existing screen. Net £2,370.00, VAT £474.00, total £2,844.00, with no line items.
That quotation states the property as 8 Wrenfold Mews, Brindlewick, ZZ1 1ZZ, which is not the case property.

Contractor's breakdown of 18 Sep gives materials £1,270 and labour £1,170 (two operatives, half a day each) = £2,440 net, plus VAT at 20% and a 'Northbridge commission at 10%', with no revised subtotal or total and no deposit basis; this does not reconcile with the £2,370 net on the quotation.
Landlord twice declined to approve pending itemisation (18 Sep) and on 23 Sep asked which quote was meant, saying there were a couple; no approval of any amount exists in the history.
No visit report or invoice is recorded on the file; the agency itself noted this on 18 Sep.

Safety check: the reported water is confined to the bathroom (grout and wall covering). No flooding, no water near electrics, no mould and no vulnerability are reported anywhere in the artefacts, so the emergency definitions are not met; the damp risk from a leak running since 04 Sep is live and the tenant has been given mould and escalation advice.
Office keys were released to the contractor for unaccompanied access; no record of their return exists.

Dear Ms Quill, an update on the leak behind the shower at your property. The plumber inspected on 18 September and has sent a quotation for the bathroom work. The figures on it do not add up against the breakdown he later gave us, so we have gone back to him for a corrected, itemised quotation; the landlord decides whether the work goes ahead and we will put the corrected figures to him as soon as we have them. We cannot give you a work date yet and we will not promise one until a booking is actually confirmed with you.
In the meantime, to limit damage: if you can, avoid using the shower and use the bath tap instead; keep the bathroom ventilated and wipe standing water from the floor and the wall covering; and do not try to seal or cut into the wall covering yourself.
Please contact us straight away if any of the following happens — water spreads outside the bathroom or through a ceiling below, water appears near a light fitting, socket or extractor fan, the leak increases, or black mould starts to appear. Any of those we will treat as an emergency.
Two things it would help to know: are you back at the property now, and may the contractor still use the office keys for the next visit, or would you prefer to be there? Nothing in this message decides who bears the cost of the work; that is not a matter we determine.
